key_insight: Generalized hydrodynamic stability analysis captures rarefaction effects missed by Navier–Stokes theory, revealing weaker acoustic–viscous mode synchronization and eventual stabilization of all modes as rarefaction increases.
engineering_relevance: The method supports stability assessment of high-speed, low-density shear flows relevant to high-altitude aerospace applications.
method: Develop temporal linear stability analysis using 13-moment generalized hydrodynamic equations with slip boundary conditions.
Compare predictions with nonlinear coupled constitutive relations and Navier–Stokes formulations.
Examine base flows, eigenspectra, mode synchronization, and disturbance growth across Mach and Knudsen numbers.
evidence_signal: For Ma = 2.5–10 and Kn = 2.7×10⁻⁵–0.07, generalized hydrodynamic base-flow predictions agree well with DSMC, while stability predictions differ considerably from Navier–Stokes results near Kn = 0.01.
watch_item: DSMC agreement is reported for base-flow profiles; it should not be interpreted as direct validation of disturbance growth rates or extrapolated beyond the studied near-continuum regime.
paper_title: A linear stability method based on generalized hydrodynamics: application to high-speed plane Couette flow beyond continuum regime
